proof: the APPLICATION acceptance proofs: the full lifecycle through the application boundary (Command → … → human decision → COMPLETED), Command idempotency, and a REAL multi-process restart proof against the isolated development database

environment.applicationDatabase: the isolated development cluster only — 127.0.0.1, created by `initdb` for this work, never the production Supabase host
environment.productionDatabase: NOT touched. The application proof never reads DATABASE_URL.
environment.transport: the real Hermes runtime adapter over the DETERMINISTIC test transport (an explicit allowTestTransport opt-in), so the proofs spend no provider turn. The live bridge proof is separate (scripts/run-persistence-proof.sh).

isolatedCluster.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 on x86_64-windows, compiled by msvc-19.44.35228, 64-bit

assertions.title: STEP 5 — the application boundary runs the whole lifecycle on a real database runs Command → Mission → Task → Actor → Capability → Runtime → Execution → Review → COMPLETED
STEP 5 — the application boundary runs the whole lifecycle on a real database returns the SAME mission for a retry, and runs nothing new
STEP 5 — the application boundary runs the whole lifecycle on a real database refuses a reused key with a DIFFERENT command (COMMAND_KEY_REUSED)
STEP 5 — the application boundary runs the whole lifecycle on a real database still creates a NEW mission for a genuinely new command
STEP 5 — the application boundary runs the whole lifecycle on a real database refuses a capability the actor is NOT assigned, with zero transport calls
STEP 5 — the application boundary runs the whole lifecycle on a real database rehydrates the finished mission through a FRESH application
STEP 5 — the application rehydrates a mission after a REAL process restart fails closed when the process has no verified durable database
STEP 5 — the application rehydrates a mission after a REAL process restart process A hands over an OPEN HUMAN DECISION and process B finishes the mission from the rows
STEP 5 — the application rehydrates a mission after a REAL process restart measures the case that does NOT work: an in-flight handle cannot be settled after a restart

howToReproduce: node scripts/dev-db.mjs up        # isolated development cluster + pre-migration schema
bash scripts/run-app-proof.sh      # runs both suites and re-writes this file
knownLimitationsRecordedByThisRun: An execution left IN FLIGHT by a process restart cannot be settled: the runtime adapter's handle bookkeeping is in-process memory and the port has no re-adoption seam. The restart suite asserts this failure and the stuck rows rather than hiding it.
The provider-side cancellation of such a handle is not confirmed, so cancelling such a mission closes the bookkeeping without pretending the provider run was stopped.
